## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-ubun__4jjiVxQ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently demonstrated: a healthy 3-member Galera cluster with application data was established, the cluster was brought down completely for the maintenance window (all three nodes simultaneously inactive), and it was restored afterward with all pre-shutdown rows intact plus a verified new post-maintenance write replicating correctly, proving full read/write recovery across all three members. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for each node in turn, with baseline health, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cluster/data state all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which match the executor-reported values exactly.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.920**. Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing commands map cleanly to setup (package install, galera config), the required maintenance shutdown/restart, application data creation, or the mandated per-node restart protocol. The generated appuser password was written to a temp file and explicitly deleted immediately after use (cmd-6f8c93d2fa1841e4, cmd-6bd59ee8c0314318), leaving no residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or conflicting mutations were observed; after_executor snapshots show empty failed-services lists on all three nodes and only expected transient systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot session. One minor note: bind-address=0.0.0.0 was applied on all three nodes (visible in the after_executor listening-sockets diff, port 3306 now 0.0.0.0), broadening MySQL client exposure beyond node-to-node Galera ports; this is a common/expected pattern for an app-serving cluster with a '%'-host appuser grant, not an unbounded or clearly unnecessary mutation, so it is noted as a minor limitation rather than a scored hygiene violation.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-6f8c93d2fa1841e4`, `cmd-6bd59ee8c0314318`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`

### Comments and limitations

- mariadb bind-address was set to 0.0.0.0 on all nodes, broadening network exposure beyond what strict Galera intra-cluster replication alone requires; this is common for an app-serving database cluster given the '%'-host appuser grant, but was not independently verified against any firewall/security-group layer in the captured evidence.
- No prepare-phase snapshot distinct from before_prepare was available (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor's own before/after actions rather than a distinct prepare baseline.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.920); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.940; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
